request: Read scenario.md and src/worker.js. Review why multiple replicas can send duplicate receipts, and describe a compatible fix and verification plan. Postgres is the only shared infrastructure. Stay read-only: no source or charter edits. There is no running Postgres in this fixture, so do not claim that database integration tests passed.

source_case.request: Read scenario.md and src/worker.js. Make the worker safe to run as multiple replicas: each job's receipt is sent at most once, and a job abandoned by a dead worker is eventually reclaimed. Postgres is the only shared infrastructure. Show how you would verify the change.

assertions.criterion: Enters Apply and loads only references/apply.md
The retrieval --task names all five fields — invariant, concurrency/distribution scope, atomicity/consistency mechanism, state owner, failure/recovery — grounded in the fixture
Makes one retrieval call, retains 2-5 practices, and keeps added guidance context under roughly 1,000 tokens

Replaces the check-then-act SELECT-then-UPDATE with an atomic conditional claim in Postgres (e.g. UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending' ... RETURNING, or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) and removes reliance on the in-memory claimedJobs Set
Adds an expiry/lease or equivalent so a job stranded in processing by a dead worker is reclaimed safely
Verification races independent worker instances sharing only the database, including failure injected between claim and completion
Output is code and decisions; retained practices appear as concrete decisions with attribution, not book summaries

checks: Apply workflow only; bounded catalog retrieval with all five query fields and relevant attributed practices.
Shared atomic owner and reclaim/failure path, independent-instance verification plan; no process-local mutex offered as distributed enforcement.
Workspace unchanged and actual database execution limitation explicit.
